'''Wolfram Weckwerth''' is a German [[biochemist]]. He is professor of molecular systems biology at the [[University of Vienna]], where he is founding chair of the Vienna Metabolomics Center.<ref name="mosys">{{cite web |title=Univ.-Prof. Dr. Wolfram Weckwerth |url=https://mosys.univie.ac.at/team/wolfram-weckwerth/ |website=Molecular Systems Biology, University of Vienna |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref> His research combines [[metabolomics]], [[proteomics]] and mathematical modelling to study how genes, environment and metabolism interact in plants, microbes and humans.<ref name="mosys" /> He is president of the Federation of European Societies of Plant Biology and of the Austrian Society of Plant Biology.<ref name="fespb">{{cite web |title=Executive Committee |url=https://fespb.org/executive-committee/ |website=Federation of European Societies of Plant Biology |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Weckwerth studied chemistry at the [[Technical University of Berlin]], completing his diploma in 1994, and received his PhD in biochemistry from the same university in 1998.<ref name="mosys" />

==Academic career==
===Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology===
In 2000 Weckwerth joined the [[Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology]] in Potsdam-Golm as a postdoctoral researcher, and from 2002 he led the research group "Integrative Proteomics and Metabolomics".<ref name="mosys" /><ref name="mpimp">{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. Wolfram Weckwerth |url=https://www.mpimp-golm.mpg.de/16545/Weckwerth_Wolfram |website=Max Planck Institute of Molecular Plant Physiology: Former Research Group Leaders |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref> At the institute he and colleagues described a process for the integrated extraction, identification and quantification of metabolites, proteins and RNA, intended to reveal their co-regulation in biochemical networks.<ref name="weckwerth2004">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W, etal |title=Process for the integrated extraction, identification and quantification of metabolites, proteins and RNA to reveal their co-regulation in biochemical networks |journal=Proteomics |year=2004 |volume=4 |issue=1 |pages=78–83 |doi=10.1002/pmic.200200500 |pmid=14730673}}</ref> He completed his habilitation in molecular plant physiology and systems biology at the [[University of Potsdam]] in 2007 and from 2007 to 2008 headed the central infrastructure systems biology laboratory of {{ill|FORSYS|de|lt=GoFORSYS}}, a systems biology programme funded by Germany's Federal Ministry of Education and Research.<ref name="mosys" />

===University of Vienna===
Weckwerth became a full professor at the University of Vienna in 2008 and founded the Department of Molecular Systems Biology (MOSYS).<ref name="mosys" /> From 2013 he headed the Department of Ecogenomics and Systems Biology,<ref name="mosys" /> and from 2013 to 2022 he headed the university's Large Instrument Facility of Mass Spectrometry in Life Sciences.<ref name="mosys" />

In 2015 he became founding chair of the Vienna Metabolomics Center (VIME),<ref name="mosys" /> an interdisciplinary centre that applies genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics to plant, microbial and biomedical research.<ref name="vime">{{cite web |title=Vienna Metabolomics Center |url=https://metabolomics.univie.ac.at/ |website=University of Vienna |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref> He was vice-head and then, from 2022 to 2024, head of the Department of Functional and Evolutionary Ecology, and has been speaker of the Faculty of Life Sciences' professorial curia since 2018.<ref name="mosys" /> Since 2025 he has headed the university's research platform on artificial-intelligence-powered personalized nutrition (AIPN).<ref name="aipn">{{cite web |title=Research platform Artificial Intelligence in personalized nutrition for disease prevention and well-being |url=https://aipn.univie.ac.at/de/ |website=University of Vienna |date=13 May 2026 |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref><ref name="fespb" />

He received professorial offers from [[Michigan State University]] (2006–2007) and the [[University of Liverpool]] (2016).<ref name="mosys" />

==Research==
Weckwerth's research addresses the relationship between genotype, environment and phenotype in plant, microbial, animal and human systems, combining [[systems theory]] with genome-scale molecular analysis.<ref name="mosys" />

===Metabolomics and systems biology===
At the Max Planck Institute, Weckwerth contributed to the Golm Metabolome Database, an open-access database of mass spectra for metabolite identification.<ref name="kopka2005">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kopka J, Schauer N, Krueger S, etal |title=GMD@CSB.DB: the Golm Metabolome Database |journal=Bioinformatics |year=2005 |volume=21 |issue=8 |pages=1635–1638 |doi=10.1093/bioinformatics/bti236 |pmid=15613389}}</ref> His 2003 review "Metabolomics in systems biology" in the ''Annual Review of Plant Biology'' discussed how metabolite profiling could be combined with systems-level modelling.<ref name="weckwerth2003">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W |title=Metabolomics in systems biology |journal=Annual Review of Plant Biology |year=2003 |volume=54 |issue=1 |pages=669–689 |doi=10.1146/annurev.arplant.54.031902.135014 |pmid=14503007 |bibcode=2003AnRPB..54..669W }}</ref> He returned to the theme in later reviews, including one on the unpredictability of metabolism and the role of metabolomics alongside next-generation sequencing (2011)<ref name="weckwerth2011b">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W |title=Unpredictability of metabolism—the key role of metabolomics science in combination with next-generation genome sequencing |journal=Analytical and Bioanalytical Chemistry |year=2011 |volume=400 |issue=7 |pages=1967–1978 |doi=10.1007/s00216-011-4948-9 |pmid=21556754 |pmc=3098350}}</ref> and one on system-theoretical principles in biology and ecology (2019).<ref name="weckwerth2019">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W |title=Toward a unification of system-theoretical principles in biology and ecology—the stochastic Lyapunov matrix equation and its inverse application |journal=Frontiers in Applied Mathematics and Statistics |year=2019 |volume=5 |article-number=29 |doi=10.3389/fams.2019.00029 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

===Systems theory and mathematical modelling===
Weckwerth has developed computational methods for inferring the structure of biological systems from genome-scale molecular data. In 2012, Sun and Weckwerth published COVAIN, a software toolbox for statistics, time-series and correlation-network analysis of metabolomics data, including inverse estimation of the differential [[Jacobian matrix and determinant|Jacobian]] from metabolite covariance data,<ref name="covain2012">{{cite journal |vauthors=Sun X, Weckwerth W |title=COVAIN: a toolbox for uni- and multivariate statistics, time-series and correlation network analysis and inverse estimation of the differential Jacobian from metabolomics covariance data |journal=Metabolomics |year=2012 |volume=8 |pages=81–93 |doi=10.1007/s11306-012-0399-3}}</ref> an approach developed further in later work from his group.<ref name="nagele2014">{{cite journal |vauthors=Nägele T, Mair A, Sun X, Fragner L, Teige M, Weckwerth W |title=Solving the differential biochemical Jacobian from metabolomics covariance data |journal=PLOS ONE |year=2014 |volume=9 |issue=4 |article-number=e92299 |doi=10.1371/journal.pone.0092299 |doi-access=free |pmid=24695071 |pmc=3977476 |bibcode=2014PLoSO...992299N }}</ref> The group has also applied Granger causality analysis to integrated GC–MS and LC–MS metabolomics data to examine the interface between primary and secondary metabolism.<ref name="doerfler2013">{{cite journal |vauthors=Doerfler H, Lyon D, Nägele T, Sun X, Fragner L, Hadacek F, etal |title=Granger causality in integrated GC–MS and LC–MS metabolomics data reveals the interface of primary and secondary metabolism |journal=Metabolomics |year=2013 |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=564–574 |doi=10.1007/s11306-012-0470-0 |pmid=23678342 |pmc=3651536 }}</ref> A later software tool, COVRECON, integrates genome-scale metabolic network reconstruction with data-driven inverse modelling.<ref name="covrecon2023">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li J, Waldherr S, Weckwerth W |title=COVRECON: automated integration of genome- and metabolome-scale network reconstruction and data-driven inverse modeling of metabolic interaction networks |journal=Bioinformatics |year=2023 |volume=39 |issue=7 |article-number=btad397 |doi=10.1093/bioinformatics/btad397 |pmid=37402625 |pmc=10356784 }}</ref> The group has also combined phosphoproteomics with metabolomics to study signalling and regulation in plants, including a 2016 study of the kinase SnRK1, the plant ortholog of [[AMP-activated protein kinase|AMPK]], as a metabolic master regulator under energy deprivation.<ref name="nukarinen2016">{{cite journal |vauthors=Nukarinen E, Nägele T, Pedrotti L, etal |title=Quantitative phosphoproteomics reveals the role of the AMPK plant ortholog SnRK1 as a metabolic master regulator under energy deprivation |journal=Scientific Reports |year=2016 |volume=6 |article-number=31697 |doi=10.1038/srep31697 |doi-access=free |pmid=27545962 |pmc=4992866 |bibcode=2016NatSR...631697N }}</ref>

His group has also applied inverse modelling to biomedical questions. A 2020 study involving the group identified the enzyme PHGDH as a metabolic checkpoint of macrophage polarization and proliferation,<ref name="wilson2020">{{cite journal |vauthors=Wilson JL, Nagele T, Linke M, etal |title=Inverse data-driven modeling and multiomics analysis reveals Phgdh as a metabolic checkpoint of macrophage polarization and proliferation |journal=Cell Reports |year=2020 |volume=30 |issue=5 |pages=1542–1552.e7 |doi=10.1016/j.celrep.2020.01.011 |pmid=32023468 |pmc=7003064}}</ref> and a 2024 study with Weckwerth as senior author reported that targeting PHGDH reversed the immunosuppressive phenotype of tumour-associated macrophages.<ref name="cai2024">{{cite journal |vauthors=Cai Z, Li W, Hager S, etal |title=Targeting PHGDH reverses the immunosuppressive phenotype of tumor-associated macrophages through alpha-ketoglutarate and mTORC1 signaling |journal=Cellular & Molecular Immunology |year=2024 |volume=21 |issue=5 |pages=448–465 |doi=10.1038/s41423-024-01134-0 |pmid=38409249 |pmc=11061172 }}</ref><ref name="lisa2024">{{cite news |title=Uni Vienna: Immune system meets cancer: Checkpoint identified to fight solid tumors |url=https://www.lisavienna.at/news/detail/uni-vienna-immune-system-meets-cancer-checkpoint-identified-to-fight-solid-tumors/ |work=LISAvienna |date=27 February 2024 |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref><ref name="eurekalert">{{cite press release |title=Immune system meets cancer: Checkpoint identified to fight solid tumors |url=https://www.eurekalert.org/news-releases/1035709 |publisher=EurekAlert! |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

Weckwerth organises the ''Philosophisch-theologisch-biologisches Seminar'' at the University of Vienna, an interdisciplinary forum on systems theory, emergence and self-organisation in biology.<ref name="ptb">{{cite web |title=Wolfram Weckwerth |url=https://ptb.univie.ac.at/ptb-konsortium/wolfram-weckwerth/ |website=Philosophisch-theologisch-biologisches Seminar, University of Vienna |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

===Green systems biology===
In a 2011 review, Weckwerth used the term "green systems biology" for an approach that links genome-, proteome- and metabolome-level data to ecosystems research and biotechnology.<ref name="gsb2011">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W |title=Green systems biology – from single genomes, proteomes and metabolomes to ecosystems research and biotechnology |journal=Journal of Proteomics |year=2011 |volume=75 |issue=1 |pages=284–305 |doi=10.1016/j.jprot.2011.07.010 |pmid=21802534}}</ref> His laboratory has applied this framework, together with inverse modelling, in ecology, evolution, development and biotechnology.<ref name="weckwerth2019" /><ref name="technology">{{cite news |last=Carrão |first=Catarina |title=Metabolomics: a "go-to" approach in systems biology |url=https://www.technologynetworks.com/analysis/articles/metabolomics-a-go-to-approach-in-systems-biology-327035 |work=Technology Networks |date=1 May 2020 |type=Sponsored content |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref> In ecology and evolution, a 2023 study that included his group reported metabolome plasticity across 241 ''Arabidopsis thaliana'' accessions and evidence for evolutionary cold-adaptation processes.<ref name="weiszmann2023">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weiszmann J, Walther D, Clauw P, Back G, Gunis J, Reichardt I, etal |title=Metabolome plasticity in 241 Arabidopsis thaliana accessions reveals evolutionary cold adaptation processes |journal=Plant Physiology |year=2023 |volume=193 |issue=2 |pages=980–1000 |doi=10.1093/plphys/kiad298 |pmid=37220420 |pmc=10517190 }}</ref> He has also presented the concept in a talk titled "Green systems biology – the need for ecological thinking in modern biology".<ref name="gsbtalk">{{cite AV media |people=Weckwerth W |title=Green systems biology – the need for ecological thinking in modern biology |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lhZUgD4nRzY |via=YouTube |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

===Plant genomics and germplasm===
As chair of the Multinational Arabidopsis Steering Subcommittee for Proteomics, Weckwerth was a co-author of a 2008 report on a proteome database resource for ''[[Arabidopsis thaliana]]'' systems biology.<ref name="masc2008">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W, etal |title=The Multinational Arabidopsis Steering Subcommittee for Proteomics assembles the largest proteome database resource for plant systems biology |journal=Journal of Proteome Research |year=2008 |volume=7 |issue=10 |pages=4209–4210 |doi=10.1021/pr800480u |pmid=18785769 |osti=983113 }}</ref> More recently he was a co-author of a 2026 study of ''[[Clusia]]'' genomes and the evolution of [[crassulacean acid metabolism]] physiotypes.<ref name="kramml2026">{{cite journal |vauthors=Kramml HM, Herpell JB, Priemer C, etal |title=Clusia genomes shed light on the evolution and diversity of crassulacean acid metabolism physiotypes |journal=Nature Communications |year=2026 |volume=17 |issue=1 |article-number=3937 |doi=10.1038/s41467-026-71958-z |doi-access=free |pmid=42086566 |pmc=13144421 |bibcode=2026NatCo..17.3937K }}</ref>

With colleagues, he proposed the concept "PANOMICS meets germplasm" in a 2020 paper, which describes integrating multi-omics data and genomic prediction with germplasm collections to identify climate-adaptive traits in crops.<ref name="panomics2020">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W, Ghatak A, Bellaire A, Chaturvedi P, Varshney RK |title=PANOMICS meets germplasm |journal=Plant Biotechnology Journal |year=2020 |volume=18 |issue=7 |pages=1507–1525 |doi=10.1111/pbi.13372 |doi-access=free |pmid=32163658 |pmc=7292548 |bibcode=2020PBioJ..18.1507W }}</ref> The term panomics extends [[pan-genome|pangenomics]] by applying genomics, proteomics and metabolomics to natural variation within a species.<ref name="panomics2020" /> Weckwerth presented the concept at the 2015 conference of the Metabolomics Society.<ref name="metab2015">{{cite journal |title=Abstracts of the 11th annual international conference of the Metabolomics Society, San Francisco, 29 June – 2 July 2015 |journal=Metabolomics |year=2015 |doi=10.1007/s11306-015-0846-z}}</ref> His group's contribution to crop-genetics collaborations, including with the [[International Maize and Wheat Improvement Center]] (CIMMYT) and the [[International Crops Research Institute for the Semi-Arid Tropics]] (ICRISAT), is centred on metabolomics, data integration and systems modelling, with work on drought resilience and nitrogen efficiency in wheat, pearl millet and chickpea.<ref name="panomics2020" /><ref name="chaturvedi2024">{{cite journal |vauthors=Chaturvedi P, Pierides I, Lopez-Hidalgo C, etal |title=Natural variation in the chickpea metabolome under drought stress |journal=Plant Biotechnology Journal |year=2024 |volume=22 |issue=12 |pages=3278–3294 |doi=10.1111/pbi.14447 |doi-access=free |pmid=39411896 |pmc=11606430 |bibcode=2024PBioJ..22.3278C }}</ref> In a 2020 sponsored interview, he described an analysis of a germplasm collection of 3,000 chickpea genotypes as "metabolic genome-wide association studies".<ref name="technology" />

A further focus is biological nitrification inhibition (BNI), a trait in which some wheat genotypes release compounds that suppress soil nitrification. Weckwerth's group has studied the metabolomic basis of this trait with CIMMYT and ICRISAT partners.<ref name="ghatak2025">{{cite journal |vauthors=Ghatak A, etal |title=Natural variation of the wheat root exudate metabolome and its influence on biological nitrification inhibition activity |journal=Plant Biotechnology Journal |year=2025 |volume=23 |issue=11 |pages=4755–4772 |doi=10.1111/pbi.70248 |doi-access=free |pmid=40692297 |pmc=12576471 |bibcode=2025PBioJ..23.4755G }}</ref><ref name="univie-holobiont">{{cite web |title=The holobiont revolution: how wheat is becoming more climate-resilient through nature-based plant breeding and machine learning |url=https://www.univie.ac.at/en/news/detail/the-holobiont-revolution-how-wheat-is-becoming-more-climate-resilient-through-nature-based-plant-breeding-and-machine-learning |website=University of Vienna |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

===Holobionts and plant–microbiome interactions===
The [[holobiont]] concept, which treats a host together with its associated microbiome as a functional unit, was developed by other researchers in microbiology and evolutionary biology. Weckwerth's recent publications apply it to plant breeding, examining natural variation in the plant holobiont and arguing that breeding strategies should take the associated microbial community into account.<ref name="ghatak2023">{{cite journal |vauthors=Ghatak A, Chaturvedi P, Waldherr S, Subbarao GV, Weckwerth W |title=PANOMICS at the interface of root-soil microbiome and BNI |journal=Trends in Plant Science |year=2023 |volume=28 |issue=1 |pages=106–122 |doi=10.1016/j.tplants.2022.08.016 |pmid=36229336 |bibcode=2023TPS....28..106G }}</ref><ref name="weckwerth2025">{{cite journal |vauthors=Weckwerth W, Chaturvedi P, Ghatak A, etal |title=Natural variation of the holobiont for sustainable agroecosystems |journal=Trends in Plant Science |year=2025 |volume=30 |issue=9 |pages=972–979 |doi=10.1016/j.tplants.2025.05.006 |pmid=40579258 |bibcode=2025TPS....30..972W }}</ref>

===Human and planetary health===
Weckwerth's group has more recently studied how plant-derived natural products affect inflammatory responses and immune function,<ref name="li2023">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li W, Cai Z, Schindler F, etal |title=Norbergenin prevents LPS-induced inflammatory responses in macrophages through inhibiting NFkappaB, MAPK and STAT3 activation and blocking metabolic reprogramming |journal=Frontiers in Immunology |year=2023 |volume=14 |at=1117638 |doi=10.3389/fimmu.2023.1117638 |doi-access=free |pmid=37251401 |pmc=10213229 }}</ref> and liver lipotoxicity,<ref name="li2024">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li W, Cai Z, Schindler F, Afjehi-Sadat L, Montsch B, Heffeter P, etal |title=Elevated PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy and boosted mitochondrial function mediate protection of HepG2 cells from excess palmitic acid by hesperetin |journal=Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry |year=2024 |volume=72 |issue=23 |pages=13039–13053 |doi=10.1021/acs.jafc.3c09132 |pmid=38809522 |pmc=11181321 |bibcode=2024JAFC...7213039L }}</ref><ref name="li2025">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li W, Cai Z, Schindler F, Brenner M, Winter C, Stiller B, etal |title=Hesperetin protects from palmitic-acid-induced lipotoxicity through the inhibition of glutaminolysis, mTORC1 signaling, and limited apoptosis |journal=Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry |year=2025 |volume=73 |issue=35 |pages=21932–21946 |doi=10.1021/acs.jafc.5c05570 |pmid=40838694 |pmc=12412169 |bibcode=2025JAFC...7321932L }}</ref> and has applied machine learning and inverse modelling to metabolomics data on active ageing.<ref name="li2025aging">{{cite journal |vauthors=Li J, Brenner M, Pierides I, etal |title=Machine learning and data-driven inverse modeling of metabolomics unveil key processes of active aging |journal=npj Systems Biology and Applications |year=2025 |volume=11 |issue=1 |article-number=103 |doi=10.1038/s41540-025-00580-4 |doi-access=free |pmid=40993122 |pmc=12460594 }}</ref> These themes underpin the AIPN research platform.<ref name="aipn" /> He has also worked on translating frameworks such as the [[EAT-Lancet Commission|EAT-Lancet report]] into personalised, data-driven dietary concepts, linking [[planetary health]] with research on human metabolism and the microbiome.<ref name="ech">{{cite web |title=From planetary diets to personalised nutrition |url=https://ech.univie.ac.at/story/from-planetary-diets-to-personalised-nutrition |website=University of Vienna |date=3 February 2026 |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref><ref name="planetarytalk">{{cite AV media |people=Weckwerth W |title=Talk introducing the "planetary health meets personalized nutrition" concept |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qJmBrmmrQF8 |via=YouTube |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref>

==Professional service==
Weckwerth is president of the Federation of European Societies of Plant Biology (FESPB), an umbrella organisation of national plant biology societies in Europe, and president of the Austrian Society of Plant Biology, one of its member societies, a post he has held since 2023.<ref name="fespb" />

He has been active in international Arabidopsis research coordination: he chaired the Multinational Arabidopsis Steering Committee, was founding chair of its proteomics subcommittee, and has chaired its metabolomics subcommittee. He is a founding member and European coordinator of the International Plant Proteomics Organization (INPPO).<ref name="mosys" /> He is the founding special chief editor of the metabolomics section of ''Frontiers'' and has served on the editorial boards of the ''Journal of Personalized Medicine'', ''Current Metabolomics'', ''Plant and Cell Physiology'' and ''Frontiers in Plant Science''.<ref name="mosys" /> He has served on scientific advisory boards including Czech Globe (2013–2015), the Austrian Society of Analytical Chemistry (2010–2012), the International Pearl Millet Genome Sequencing Consortium at ICRISAT (since 2016) and ''Open Science – Lebenswissenschaften im Dialog'' in Vienna (since 2010),<ref name="mosys" /><ref name="openscience">{{cite web |title=Open Science – Lebenswissenschaften im Dialog |url=https://www.openscience.or.at/en/ |website=Open Science – Lebenswissenschaften im Dialog |access-date=11 November 2026}}</ref> and on European Research Council evaluation panels (2022–2025).<ref name="mosys" />
